body: Does the docker succeed if it has gpu access for blender?
As far as I know this feature is only available for NVIDIA GPUs. That I can not test, because on my personal computer I have an AMD, and on my CI/CD pipepline I just have intel iGPU.

Happening to me as well with .GLB files on Ubuntu 24.04 Server on bare metal, tried reinstalling the OS, and also tried it on Linux Mint 22.1 in case a desktop environment would fix anything.

Engine version: Godot v4.4.1-stable
CPU: Intel N100
GPU: Intel UHD Graphics (integrated)
RAM: 8GB DDR4

Freezes indefinitely (at least 6 hours) on importing. Used GDB to debug editor and got the stack trace below

Happens with headless & with regular rendering

Based on the stack trace, it looks like a deadlock, which is not new for the importing process

Potentially related:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94586
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94910
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104013

Command used: `xvfb-run godot --import`

Are you guys still able to replicate it with the blend files?

In case anyone else is running into this as well, I was able to get around this issue by doing the following:
1. Downloading a compatible version of Blender
2. Adding `blender` to `~/.config/godot/editor_settings-4.*.tres`
3. Installing various xorg-related packages (on Ubuntu this was `apt install xorg xz-utils xvfb`)

Before running the above steps, I ensured the editor settings file was generated via calling:
```sh
godot -v -e --quit --headless
```

I also ensured that `filesystem/import/blender/rpc_port` and `filesystem/import/blender/rpc_server_uptime` were defined in the same file too.
